story: Saturday evening in Sumter Oaks finds the humid October air hanging thick over Magnolia Loop, where Donna is cheerfully making her way toward Rosa's House while Rosa herself is strolling the same direction. Inside Rosa's kitchen, Gary is content to have the ice set out for the table, and Hal arrives gruffly but warmly, praising Gary for keeping his golf cart parked until the board signs off and asking where he can help with the carrying.
events: Gary (rosa kitchen): Carry the ice into the kitchen and set it out for the table

gary.thought_process: I'm at Rosa's with Hal nearby, and Rosa told me to grab the ice and follow them to the kitchen. The table's set and the cobbler's warming, so this is the moment to be useful. I asked nobody anything this tick, and the cart can wait until the review board signs off. Easiest way to feel needed tonight is to get the ice where it belongs and sit down to dinner with good people.

parameters.content: Carry the ice into the kitchen and set it out for the table

donna.thought_process: Rosa just told me to bring the cobbler straight through to the kitchen, and Hal and Gary are already headed in. Nothing more to ask or confirm. I've already invited Gary to hit dinks tomorrow, so no need to nag him again. The sensible thing is to walk over to Rosa's with the cobbler and join the dinner, which keeps me at the center of the gathering.

parameters.content: Taking the peach cobbler over to Rosa's dinner, as she asked.

hal.thought_process: Gary just walked in carrying ice and drinks, and he already told Rosa the cart's staying in the garage till the review board signs off. That's the by-the-book behavior I like to see, and I shouldn't gripe about it tonight. I'm here for Rosa's dinner, and I've been meaning to get that cornbread and table squared away. Rosa's table already has cornbread on it, so I'll give Gary a short, civil word and then pitch in. Fewer words, more work.

parameters.content: Evening, Gary. Heard you kept the cart parked till the board signs off. That's how it's done. Now point me at whatever needs carrying.

rosa.thought_process: Hal is already at my house, Donna and Gary are walking over together, and I'm standing out on Magnolia Loop at 8:17 PM. The dinner is waiting and the last guests are on their way. Donna is right here, and I just told her to go straight in, so I shouldn't repeat myself. The best thing is to head back inside and get everyone seated and fed.

parameters.content: Heading back inside to get everyone seated and serve dinner at my long table.

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
